reason: The sources provide sufficient corroborated data to create a compelling 45-second short on rogue planets.
story: Picture a planet completely detached from any star, drifting through eternal darkness in the Milky Way. Astronomers call them rogue planets. Instead of orbiting a sun, these cosmic nomads roam the galaxy in total solitude. Some formed on their own from collapsing gas clouds, while others were violently flung out of their home systems by giant sibling planets during chaotic early impacts. Without a star to warm them, they are freezing, pitch-black, and nearly impossible to detect. Yet, they are shockingly common. Scientists estimate there are billions or even trillions of these starless worlds wandering through our galaxy, outnumbering stars. Thanks to gravitational microlensing and upcoming space telescopes like NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, we are finally uncovering these invisible drifters, challenging everything we thought we knew about planetary systems and where life might find a spark.
angle: Billions to trillions of starless rogue planets drift through total darkness in the Milky Way, outnumbering stars.

claims.claim: Rogue planets are free-floating planetary-mass objects not gravitationally bound to any star or brown dwarf.
The Milky Way alone may have billions to trillions of rogue planets.
In December 2021, astronomers discovered a group of at least 70 and up to 170 rogue planets in the OB association between Upper Scorpius and Ophiuchus.
Rogue planets can form either through direct gravitational collapse within stellar nurseries or through ejection from their natal planetary systems.
Gravitational microlensing occurs when a massive foreground object aligns with a background star, warping spacetime and magnifying the star's light.
Microlensing events caused by rogue planets typically last between a few hours and a couple of days.
In September 2020, astronomers reported the detection for the first time of an Earth-mass rogue planet named OGLE-2016-BLG-1928.
NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will use microlensing to monitor hundreds of millions of stars and reveal hundreds of rogue planets.
An Earth-sized ejected planet with radioactive core isotope decay could maintain a surface temperature above the melting point of water, allowing liquid-water oceans.
Moons orbiting ejected rogue planets can generate interior heat through tidal heating caused by eccentric gravitational pulls.

disputed: The exact total count of the 2021 discovery in Upper Scorpius and Ophiuchus ranges between 70 and 170 depending on the assumed age and brightness of the region.

Estimates of the total population ratio vary, with some studies suggesting nearly two Jupiter-mass rogue planets per star, others suggesting up to 100,000 times more rogue planets than stars using smaller hypothetical objects, and others indicating an upper limit of 0.25 planets per main-sequence star.
